newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse strongly ahead.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse strongly ahead.

text.p: German share market confounded expectations on Monday and finished bourse trade sharply higher, with rumours of the death of the bull run appearing somewhat exaggerated.
The 30-share DAX index of German blue-chips ended the day 2.09 percent higher, gaining 67.95 points to end the session at 3,312.88 points.
Over the session, dealers played catch-up with Wall Street's firm close last Friday.

"What we are seeing is the typical short-squeeze," said one trader. The index also managed to hold onto strong gains over the session. Dealers earlier thought that gains might fall victim to profit-taking.
The Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street ended the session on Friday up 48.72 points at 6,526.07, successfully shaking off an earlier beating inflicted by jobs data.
Dealers said the market was ignoring the suggestions of inflationary pressures presented by the unemployment report.
For the rest of the day's trade, much will depend on what happens once Wall Street opens, dealers said.

Chemical group BASF AG, still benefitting from an upbeat outlook for the current year, was among the most heavily traded stocks on Monday, ending the day up 2.30 marks, around 3.6 percent, at 65.95 marks.
BASF's rivals Bayer AG and Hoechst AG also performed well, with Bayer ending up 2.21 points, or 3.31 percent, at 68.80 marks and Hoechst ending up 1.60 marks, or 2.46 percent, at 66.60 marks.
